updates.statement: The number of epochs needed to reach 75% (sample efficiency) sets most of the wall time. Backbone, optimizer and regularization choices that cut epochs-to-target are the main lever. Together with resizing and compile, they give about 10x over the 40-epoch ResNet9 baseline (59.3 s → 6.02 s at E026).
updates.reason: Bookkeeping: the 7x figure is out of date; the tip is now 6.02 s. Every child result is still consistent with the claim.

The only support is E006: one unreplicated 3-seed run that changed batch size 1024→2000 and the optimizer together, on a fresh RNG stream. The only public CIFAR-100 recipe found Muon worse than SGD at every size (search: iterate-futurebiohackers). H1.2.2 is the decisive ablation and has never been run.
The evidence token should be E006~, not E006+. E006 measured neither epochs-to-target nor an SGD baseline tuned at batch 2000, so it did not test this prediction (review).

PreciseBN (search: 2105.07576) supports both the mechanism (EMA BN stats lag fast-moving weights, and averaged weights have mismatched buffers) and the 10^3–10^4-sample budget, but expects 0.1–0.3 pp. Three members expect it to be refuted, so the 0.2 pp threshold is a genuine test. It has been 'next' since E005 without being run.
The airbench paper (search: 2404.00498v2) reports a larger speedup from alternating flip without TTA (27%) than with TTA (21%). Still untested locally, so it stays open.

H1.5.1's support shrank to +0.24 pp held-out across a build change. E022 (wd ×0.25) went the wrong way. E013 and E014 were unreadable 3-seed nulls. All four members vote refuted. Lowered, not closed: H1.5.7 is the clean test.

E016's 3-seed +0.33 pp was lucky by +0.43 pp. Held-out, E016 (0.7564) vs E010 (0.7540) is +0.24 pp. That is below the stated 0.3 pp threshold, about 2.4σ, and it crosses a change from no-cudagraphs to max-autotune. The evidence token should be E016~.

Synced with the verdict file (supports). E010 cut time 4.8% for −0.25 pp on 3 seeds, and E012's held-out mean of 0.7540 is consistent. Only moderate confidence because the accuracy loss was read from 3 seeds.

updates.statement: On the E026 tip, lowering label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.1 (near Hiverge's 0.09) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp at unchanged time.
updates.reason: Rebased to the tip. Hiverge uses LS 0.09, but that was tuned for a 10-class problem, and three members expect it to be refuted.
All four members expect it to be refuted, and E014's trend was within noise. Run it only after H1.2.2 shows that Muon is worth keeping.

updates.statement: Paired single-factor test: on the E026 tip, restoring wd ×1 (from ×0.5) lowers the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp compared with 0.7541.
updates.reason: Rebased to the tip. It decides whether the wd change (H1.5.1) is a real lever or a lucky draw. Time-neutral.
Evidence fix: E004 (−14% time, bit-identical accuracy) is the supporting run, so the token should be E004+. E003~ was confounded by a recompile leak.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial for tile-friendly sizes (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). Accuracy is carried by the 28 and 32 px phases. E007's 24/28/32 at 40/30/30 is cheap, and so is a short early 20 px phase (E026: −0.15 pp held-out, unresolved). Removing the 28 px phase (E018: −0.68 pp held-out), shrinking the 32 px share to 20% (E011: −0.97 pp on 3 seeds, confounded with the 20 px start) or using off-grid sizes (E024: 26 px, −0.25 pp for −2%) costs more accuracy per second than the epoch dial. Candidate mechanisms: (a) low resolution during the peak-LR window; (b) a FixRes object-scale and BN-statistics shift at the final jump; (c) too little full-resolution fine-tuning while LR decays and averaging forms (C0011).
updates.reason: The statement was 'supported' while its evidence tokens were refutations, so it now states the supported part (E007-style resizing and an early low-res start are cheap) and records the refuted aggressive variants as boundary results. This explains the E011, E018 and E024 counterexamples. The E011 attribution was worked out by subtraction across bases and is flagged as unmeasured.

The accuracy clause held (−0.15 pp held-out vs E023, inside the noise floor). The time clause missed: −2.9% vs the ≥4% required, because the base was really E023 (9.0 true epochs, time 6.20 s), not E016 as the description says. That base mix-up also explains why E026's time fell outside every forecaster's range. The practical finding (an early 20 px phase is cheap) stands. Verify the step count in commit ac32d27.
Tied to the discarded E018 schedule. H1.3.6 on the tip tests the same BN-recalibration mechanism more usefully. Kept as a cheap offline follow-up.

The MosaicML card warns of harm on short schedules and needs ≥33% of examples dropped to pay off. Loss-based selection degrades on ambiguous labels, which CIFAR-100 has many of (2107.07741). The airbench96_faster proxy only paid off over 45 epochs. Two members vote refuted.
The fixed cost of training a separate proxy cannot amortize in about 9 epochs (search: airbench96_faster). All four members expect it to be refuted. H2.4.2 covers the cheaper variant.
These are the exact MosaicML settings, which gave about 8–10% in 100+ epoch runs, and the card flags short schedules as a risk. All four members expect it to be refuted. Low priority.
E021 refuted the group-2 width cut (−0.50 pp held-out for −7.8%). The assumption that conv FLOPs dominate has never been profiled, and all four members vote refuted. Profile first (H2.2.4/H6.1.1).
Three members expect it to be refuted. The late-epoch removal of high-resolution work may hurt as much as E018/E021. Do not run before the profiler trace.
FreezeOut worked for residual nets in 100-epoch CIFAR-100 runs but not for VGG-like nets. Airbench groups have limited skip connections. Drop-Muon showed only small CIFAR-10 gains (search).
In about 9 epochs the early layers are still learning late in training (search: FreezeOut, Drop-Muon). Three members expect it to be refuted. Profile group-1 backward cost first.
Strengthened: the population margin at the tip is now only about 0.11 pp held-out (E026), and every recent trim has been decided by whether it stays above the bar.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has three parts. (a) Rebuild noise: no-cudagraph artifacts are bit-identical per seed, and max-autotune/cudagraph rebuilds move the 3-seed mean only about ±0.03 pp (E019). (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed std is 0.15–0.32 pp, so the 3-seed mean SE is about 0.14 pp. (c) Trajectory re-draw: any change to the math or to random-number use re-draws every seed independently, so seeds do not pair across recipes. This holds even for a single scalar such as the Lookahead exponent (E025: seeds 0–2 +0.19 pp, held-out −0.27 pp). Offsets of the seeds 0–2 mean from the held-out mean have RMS of about 0.25–0.4 pp (E016 +0.43, E017 −0.40). The difference of two 10-seed held-out means has SE ≈0.10 pp, with an empirical floor of 0.13 pp (E016 vs E017, identical distributions). Decisions need at least 2–2.5σ or a replicate on seeds 13–22. Single 3-seed differences under about 0.5 pp cannot be interpreted.
updates.reason: E025 contradicts the old part (c) (re-roll only when RNG use changes). The review's chaotic-divergence model fits all the data, and the SE figure is corrected for the lack of pairing.

E019 already answered it: rebuilds move the 3-seed mean only ±0.03 pp. E025 shows the offset is re-drawn by any math change, not only by RNG-stream changes, so this test no longer separates the hypotheses that matter (review).

updates.statement: Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial: about 0.3–0.45 pp of held-out accuracy and about 0.68 s per true epoch, i.e. about 1.5–2.2 s/pp. The slope is 0.44 using E017's 9.5-epoch point (0.7577) and 0.31 using E016's equivalent point (0.7564). Exchange rates of the other dials (E026 ≈1.2, E021 ≈1.0, E018 ≈0.8, E024 ≈0.5 s/pp) have wide intervals at 0.10 pp SE; E026's spans roughly 0.7–3.6 s/pp. Only E011 and E018 are clearly worse than the epoch dial. Choose among dials with overlapping intervals by time saved, subject to the population mean staying above the bar.
updates.reason: The review showed the 0.44 pp/epoch slope depends on which 9.5-epoch point is used, and that ranking dials by their s/pp ratios goes beyond the data.

Partly refuted. The slope clause held: −0.21 pp held-out per 0.5 epoch for −5.3% time (E023), and −0.44 pp at −1.0 epoch (E020). The pre-registered 3-seed clause (≥0.7545) failed: E023 got 0.7538. It was wrongly logged as support.

Rests entirely on E006's confounded batch-size + optimizer change. LLM studies (2505.02222, 2507.01598) weakly support Muon's large critical batch but do not cover CIFAR CNNs. Kept at or below 0.3 until H1.2.2 and H5.1.x are run (review).
Two members vote refuted and none support. The external evidence comes only from LLMs. FFCV-style batch sizes per resolution phase add a variant (new child).

updates.statement: On the E026 tip at the same true epoch count, raising batch from 2000 to 2500 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, schedules stretched to the new step count) keeps the held-out seeds 3–12 mean within 0.15 pp of 0.7541 and cuts mean time by at least 1.5%.
updates.reason: Rebased to the tip. All four members expect it to be refuted, since per-step overhead is only about 5% (E011). It is a decisive test of H5.1's large-batch half.
All four members expect it to be refuted. Hiverge's batch of 1536 is a CIFAR-10 data point only. Rebase it to the E026 tip when it is run.

Three members vote refuted, and E011's near pixel-proportional scaling argues against a large gap. However, E021 and E024 show shape-dependent inefficiency that no profiler has measured yet (new child H6.2). Kept open until the trace exists.

new.statement: Kernel efficiency depends on whether feature-map and channel sizes align with tensor-core tiles. Tile-friendly shapes (24/28/32 px → maps 23/11/5, 27/13/6, 31/15/7; channels in multiples of 128) scale with pixels/MACs. Off-grid shapes (26 px → maps 25/12/6; 320 channels) realise only about half of their predicted saving. This explains the E024 time counterexample (−2.0% vs −4.4% modelled) and E021's sublinear MAC scaling (−15.5% MACs, −7.8% time).

A per-layer torch.profiler trace of the E026 tip shows achieved conv TFLOP/s at 26 px at least 15% below the mean of 24 and 28 px for group-2/3 layers, while 20/24/28/32 px stay within 10% of one another per layer.

An early low resolution is close to free. On the E026 tip, extending the 20 px phase from 15% to 30% of steps (taken from the 24 px phase; the 28/32 px phases keep their step counts and positions) cuts mean time by at least 2.5% and loses no more than 0.15 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean.

The 32 px share carries accuracy. E011's loss was attributed to it only by subtraction across bases. On the E026 tip, moving 10% of steps from the 24 px phase to the 32 px phase (20/24/28/32 at 15/15/30/40) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.25 pp for no more than +6% time. That rate would match or beat the epoch dial.

Non-uniform trims beat uniform ones. On the E026 tip, saving about 0.34 s (the time of a uniform −0.5 epoch trim) by removing only 20/24 px steps (28/32 px step counts unchanged; LR and EMA schedules stretched) loses no more than 0.1 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean, about half the uniform trim's −0.21 pp (E023).

The tip's margin is real. Run offline on fresh seeds 13–22, the E026 recipe gives a mean within 0.15 pp of its seeds 3–12 mean (0.7541), and the pooled 20-seed mean is at least 0.753 (SE about 0.05 pp).

The triangular LR schedule (warm-up then linear decay), copied from CIFAR-10 airbench, is mis-timed relative to the resolution phases: the peak-LR window falls in the 20/24 px phases and the decay overlaps the 28/32 px phases. Re-timing the warm-up length and peak position (and the EMA start) relative to the resolution schedule raises accuracy per epoch at zero time cost.

On the E026 tip, halving the LR warm-up fraction (peak earlier, same peak value, linear decay to the same floor), with everything else unchanged, raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp. Hiverge uses no warm-up at all.

Less frequent fast-weight resets help. E025 showed a harder pull hurts, so on the E026 tip, raising the Lookahead interval from every 5 to every 10 steps (alpha per update rescaled so the total pull per step is unchanged, final full copy kept) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at unchanged time.

Two-stage label smoothing: on the E026 tip, keeping LS 0.3 for the first 85% of steps and setting it to 0 for the final 15% (where the Lookahead average forms) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at unchanged time.

On the E026 tip, adding Hiverge-style brightness/contrast jitter on the GPU (ranges about 0.14/0.13), with everything else unchanged, raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at no more than +1% time. The prior is low because short CIFAR-100 runs are under-fitting, and extra augmentation may hurt.

Batch size per resolution phase: on the E026 tip, using batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, step counts recomputed) and 2000 at 28/32 px cuts mean time by at least 2% and keeps the held-out seeds 3–12 mean within 0.15 pp of 0.7541.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E026: 6.02 s, with a held-out mean of 0.7541. That is only about 0.11 pp above the 0.753 bar, so the next time cut has to be paid for with an accuracy gain.

**Noise model (H4.1, H4.2).**
- H4.1 is rewritten. Any recipe change re-draws every seed (E025 shows this), so seeds don't pair across recipes. The difference of two 10-seed held-out means has SE ≈0.10 pp, with an empirical floor of 0.13 pp.
- H4.2's epoch slope is widened to 0.3–0.45 pp/epoch. Its s/pp exchange rates now carry wide intervals.
- H4.1.4 is retired because E019 already answered it.
- H4.2.4 is marked inconclusive: the slope held, but its pre-registered 3-seed clause failed.

**Attribution downgrades.**
- H1.5.1 (wd) is now inconclusive: only +0.24 pp held-out, across a build change.
- H1.2.1's E006 token should be read as `~` (inconclusive).
- H1.2 and H5 are lowered, because Muon's gain rests on E006 alone and a public CIFAR-100 recipe found Muon worse than SGD.
- H1.2.2 is rebased to the tip and becomes the decisive ablation.
- Searches and members expect these to fail, so they are lowered or retired: data selection (H2.4, H2.4.1), FreezeOut (H2.6), architecture cuts (H2.5), cheaper Newton–Schulz steps for Muon (H1.2.3), Muon lr ×2 (H1.5.6), and the stale LR-floor and label-smoothing tests (H1.3.4, H1.3.1).

**Bookkeeping fixes.**
- H1.5.2 is synced to supported.
- H2.2.1's evidence should point to E004.
- H2.3 is rewritten to the supported claim: E007-style resizing and an early 20 px phase are cheap, but cutting the 28/32 px share is not. This explains the E011, E018 and E024 counterexamples.
- H2.3.2 is inconclusive. Its time clause missed (−2.9% vs the ≥4% required) because the base was really E023, not E016. That base mix-up also explains why E026's time fell outside every forecaster's range.
- H1 is updated to about 10x.

**Counterexamples.**
- E016: a lucky seeds 0–2 draw (H4.1).
- E011, E018: the 28/32 px phases carry accuracy (H2.3).
- E024: off-grid shapes tile poorly (new H6.2 and H6.2.1).
- E025: a harder pull on the fast weights hurts. H1.3 is reframed as reducing end-point variance without disturbing the fast-weight trajectory. Its time miss was a forecast-base error.
- E026: the forecast-base error described above.

**New tests,** all time-neutral or accuracy-buying and judged on held-out seeds:
- Lookahead resets every 10 steps instead of 5 (H1.3.7).
- Two-stage label smoothing (H1.3.8).
- Colour jitter (H1.5.8).
- A new branch on LR schedule timing relative to the resolution phases (H1.6, H1.6.1).
- A longer early 20 px phase (H2.3.6).
- A longer 32 px tail (H2.3.7).
- A non-uniform epoch trim (H4.2.5).
- A seeds 13–22 replicate of the tip's margin (H4.3.2).
- Batch size per resolution phase (H5.1.3).

**Priority order:**
1. BN recompute (H1.3.6) and plain EMA vs Lookahead (H1.3.5), the cheap end-point levers.
2. wd ×1 on the tip (H1.5.7) and SGD instead of Muon (H1.2.2), the attribution tests.
3. One profiler trace (H2.2.4, H6.1.1, H6.2.1) before any more architecture or backward-truncation work.

H5 and H6 remain open at Lvl1.
